processState.note: P10 did not attach to, focus, navigate or alter the already-running browser.

narrator.finding: No reliable Narrator utterance stream or speech-viewer/transcript interface was discovered in the bounded local inspection. Narrator is not running, so there is no real speech output to capture in this session.

uiaAutomation.capabilityBoundary: UIA can observe accessibility names, roles, states, focus/property/structure events and support synchronized semantic evidence. It does not prove or expose the exact sentence Narrator actually speaks, its ordering, verbosity, pronunciation or interruption behavior.

audioCaptureReadiness.endpointCaution: The observed virtual microphone was not tested and must not be assumed to be a Narrator/system-audio loopback endpoint. WASAPI render-loopback capability is conceptually available through Windows Core Audio even when no loopback capture endpoint is listed, but it was not exercised by P10.
audioCaptureReadiness.finding: Real audio waveform capture could be engineered later with an authorized WASAPI loopback helper, but no ready local capture+transcription chain exists now. Audio alone would still require authoritative transcription/verification and synchronized interaction evidence.

findings: D15 uses a role=tablist with five role=tab elements and five role=tabpanel elements.
aria-controls and aria-labelledby pair tabs and panels; the selected tab has aria-selected=true and roving tabindex=0 while inactive tabs use -1.
ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End are owned by the D15 tab binder and move focus to the newly selected tab.
Instructor-panel focus prevents global FCV keyboard shortcut routing.
Native Enter/Space button activation is not duplicated by FCV shortcut routing.
Off-device semantic changes use polite atomic role=status live regions; the LCD is intentionally not a global aria-live surface.
d15StaticReadiness.claimBoundary: These source semantics make a native Narrator run meaningful but do not predict exact spoken text, speech order, verbosity, pronunciation or timing.

whyBlocked: Narrator is intentionally not running and P10 is prohibited from launching it.
A valid spoken-output test requires interactive keyboard/focus traversal; P10 is prohibited from changing desktop focus.
UI Automation exposes semantic accessibility data and focus/property events, not Narrator's actual utterance stream.
No local Narrator speech-viewer/transcript facility was found in the bounded environment.
No ready system-audio recorder/loopback CLI or Python audio capture stack was found; Core Audio loopback would require a future helper and explicit run authorization.
No local ASR stack was found; even if installed later, ASR output alone would not be authoritative evidence of exact Narrator speech because recognition errors can differ from emitted speech.
The page is Vietnamese while locally enumerated OneCore/SAPI voices are en-US; exact pronunciation/utterance must therefore be observed, not inferred.
feasibilityAnalysis.forbiddenFallback: Do not convert DOM text, aria-labels, UIA Name properties or live-region source strings into a claimed Narrator transcript. Those are expected semantics, not observed speech.

principles: Use an isolated QA desktop session and a QA-owned loopback web port; never reuse or alter user port 4173.
Bind the run to exact canonical source hashes, Windows build, Narrator binary hash/version, browser version and Narrator configuration/voice observed before traversal.
Start Narrator manually or by an explicitly authorized operator action; do not silently alter Narrator/Windows accessibility settings.

Traverse a short predetermined keyboard path: D15 five tabs using Tab/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End, representative live-region transitions, and selected device buttons whose accessible labels are already source-defined.
Capture synchronized UIA FocusChanged/property events with timestamps to prove which accessible object had focus when speech occurred; UIA remains corroborating evidence, not the transcript source.

Capture Narrator/system render audio through a dedicated WASAPI loopback recorder if a future helper is approved; write to an isolated QA evidence path and keep unrelated application audio silent to reduce privacy/attribution ambiguity.
Create the transcript from the captured audio and human-verify it against the waveform/screen interaction. ASR may assist but must not be the sole acceptance oracle.
Record duplicate/missing announcements, interruption behavior and live-region timing explicitly; a source-label match alone is insufficient.
If loopback audio cannot be isolated without changing user audio settings, stop and return BLOCKED rather than changing endpoints or using microphone audio without authorization.
minimumPassEvidence: actual audio file containing Narrator output
synchronized UIA focus/property event log or equivalent interaction timeline
operator path and expected-versus-observed utterance table
explicit statement that no DOM-derived text was substituted for missing speech

noninvasiveNextSteps.action: Keep Narrator spoken-output status BLOCKED/NOT_RUN and retain current static DOM/UIA evidence only.

If a future native run is approved, first prepare and independently review a small write-once WASAPI-loopback + UIA-event capture helper without executing it; the helper must not change endpoints, volume, accessibility settings or browser focus by itself.
Only after explicit interactive authorization, have the operator start Narrator and perform the bounded keyboard traversal while the approved helper records system-render audio and UIA events.
Human-verify the transcript from actual captured audio; if audio isolation, capture or transcript verification fails, preserve BLOCKED instead of inferring speech from the accessibility tree.
